rationale: PINS the SOURCE of a channel operation inside a FUNC LITERAL that initializes a NAMED PACKAGE-SCOPE var — the shape go/closure-channel-read does not cover, and the one that was wrong. `findContainingGoFunction` walks up for a `function_declaration` or `method_declaration` only, so a func literal had no containing function and the channel pass's `?? "global"` fallback answered a pseudo-source for work a named declaration owns: `var Handler = func() int { <-Ch; ... }` published `uses global -> Ch` instead of `Handler -> Ch`. Same shape as GOD11 (package-scope var attributed to `global`), the package-scope `instantiates` site, and the declared-type `resolveSource` gap through a func literal: one pass resolved the named ancestor and another fell through. THE RULE THE FIX IMPLEMENTS, stated because two narrower rules were tried and both were wrong: a func literal does not STOP the walk, it only stops it when the literal is the initializer of a NAMED PACKAGE-SCOPE var. A literal inside a function must keep climbing to its FUNCTION — the first cut stopped there and returned the LOCAL var's name, which LocalsAreNotSymbols makes an invalid source, and go/closure-channel-read failed with `closureInsideFunction -> c` missing until the climb-through was restored. A literal that is a call argument or a return value reaches the file and answers undefined, so the callers' own fallback applies. THE FOUR EXPECTED ROWS: (1) `Handler -> Ch` receive at :24 is the defect's own witness — a receive in a package-scope closure attributed to the closure's var. (2) `Sender -> Ch` send at :29 is the other operation type, so the fix is pinned for sends as well as receives. (3) `sendsAndReceives` is deliberately NOT in this file; the function case is pinned by go/closure-channel-read and duplicating it here would assert nothing new. (4) The CONTROL is the blank-identifier var: `var _ = func() int { <-Ch; ... }` at :35 has no name to attribute to, so `global -> Ch` is the honest answer and is pinned as an EXPECTED row rather than left implicit — a fix that claimed a name for `_` would fail here. NOT PINNED: confidence and tier (every channel-op row is 0.8/usage_contextual regardless of source, so pinning them asserts nothing about the attribution), and the `contains`/`exports` rows this file also produces (owned by other passes).

expectRelationships.comment: A receive inside a package-scope func literal attributes to the named var that owns it.
The send half of the same construct: the rule covers both operation types.
CONTROL: a blank-identifier var has no name to attribute to, so `global` is the honest answer. A fix that claimed a name for `_` would fail here.

forbidRelationships.comment: `global` is forbidden for the NAMED package-scope closure: that is the defect this fixture exists to prevent. Before the fix this exact row was published and the closure's own name was absent.
`global` is forbidden for the named send closure for the same reason.
A blank-identifier var cannot be the source of anything: `_` never resolves. Attributing the closure's read to a name the file does not declare would be worse than the pseudo-source.
